description: 1-Wire (Maxim/Dallas standard speed and overdrive) slot receiver over measured level intervals, one interval per accepted beat, that assembles bytes LSB-first and folds the running CRC8/MAXIM of the transaction. a[15:0]=the interval length in microseconds, a[16]=the line level (1=high, 0=low), a[31:17] must be zero. b[15:0] must be zero. c[7:0]=REC_MIN, the minimum high recovery microseconds after a slot (0 disables that check), c[15:8] must be zero, c[23:16]=BYTE_LIMIT, the number of bytes accepted before the transaction is declared over-long (0 means no limit), c[29:24] must be zero, c[30]=1 selects the overdrive window set, c[31]=1 clears the shift register, bit position, byte count, CRC, pending slot and every counter before this beat is processed. Standard-speed windows: a low interval of 480..539 us is a reset with no presence pulse, 540..720 us is a reset with the published 60..240 us presence merged into it, 721 us and above is a stuck-low violation, 1..15 us is a pending 1, 60..120 us is a pending 0, 16..59 us is a short-slot violation and 121..479 us is a long-slot violation. Overdrive divides the same set to 30..53 reset without presence, 54..150 reset with presence, above 150 stuck, 1..6 pending 1 and 8..17 pending 0, with the same gap violations. A pending slot is resolved only by the following high interval: its length must be at least REC_MIN and the full slot (that low time plus the high time) must be 60..150 us (8..21 us overdrive), and only then is the pending bit accepted. A low interval arriving while a slot is still pending discards that slot and is a violation. An accepted bit shifts in LSB-first; the eighth bit completes a byte, increments the byte count, XORs the byte into the running CRC8/MAXIM (polynomial 0x31 reflected as 0x8C, init 0, no xorout) and compares the byte against the published master command set 0x33 SEARCH_ROM, 0x0F SKIP_ROM, 0xCC PRESENT, 0xA5 SEARCH_ALG, 0x96 MATCH_ROM, 0x69 READ_ROM, 0x3C OVERDRIVE_MATCH and 0xEC OVERDRIVE_SKIP. A reset clears the CRC, the byte count, the shift register and the bit position because the CRC covers exactly one transaction. A window violation, a reset without presence, a recovery violation or a byte that would exceed BYTE_LIMIT faults; an over-long byte is not folded into the CRC and is not counted. result[7:0]=the byte shift register after the beat (a whole byte on its eighth bit), result[15:8]=the running CRC after the beat, result[16]=a bit was accepted, result[17]=a byte was completed, result[18]=a reset was detected, result[19]=a presence pulse was seen, result[20]=a reset without presence, result[21]=the byte is a known master command, result[22]=a slot window violation, result[23]=restart applied, result[27:24]=the bit position, result[28]=a slot is pending, result[29]=this beat line level, result[30]=recovery violation, result[31]=transaction over-long. aux[7:0]=bytes since the last reset, aux[15:8]=the resolved slot total, aux[23:16]=the pending low interval, aux[24]=overdrive mode, aux[25]=stuck-low violation, aux[27:26]=0, aux[31:28]=violation count [3:0]. State: shift state[7:0], bit position state[11:8], CRC state[19:12], byte count state[27:20], pending low time state[43:28], pending flag state[44], pending bit value state[45], last completed byte state[53:46], saturating violation count state[61:54], saturating byte total state[69:62], saturating reset count state[77:70], saturating presence count state[85:78], saturating bit count state[93:86], saturating beat count state[101:94].
hardware_advantage: Presence, short-slot and long-slot legality are parallel window compares on the measured interval and the eighth bit folds a whole CRC8 byte through an XOR tree, so a 1-Wire transaction resolves on the enabled edge that reports it instead of a CPU busy-waiting through 60 microsecond bit bangers.
